summary: Chamcha Market in the Loang Him Kao community is a relaxed weekend outing east of Chiang Mai: browse maker-run craft stalls beneath rain trees, then pause for drip coffee and homemade bakery. A recent market walk found 49 stalls, including coffee-and-craft spaces, a bakery and several food vendors. It is a good half-day change of pace from Nimman café hopping, provided you plan a car or taxi ride.
whyGo: Pair shopping for handmade goods, cotton and indigo textiles with coffee and cake in one leafy setting.
Recent stall observations name Mama Tasty for homemade bakery and drip coffee, plus COFFEE CRAFT SPACE and Coffee Phi Ba for distinctive coffee stops.
The covered food court and northern food stalls make it easy to extend coffee into a casual snack or early lunch.
bestFor: A slow Saturday or Sunday morning with craft browsing and café breaks.
Travelers interested in local makers, textiles and casual food rather than a formal workshop itinerary.
Couples, friends or families who are comfortable walking around an outdoor market.
skipIf: You cannot visit on a weekend; the market is listed as Saturday and Sunday only.
You need a guaranteed café menu, fixed workshop or fully indoor activity.
You want a dense specialty-coffee crawl in central Chiang Mai; the main draw here is the combined market setting.
duration: Allow 1–2 hours at the market, or about half a day including the round trip from the Old City and a relaxed snack; planning estimates.
cost: No market admission charge was listed in the sources reviewed; budget separately for drinks, food, transport and shopping. A Mot Dang walk on 27 September 2026 transcribed Mama Tasty's iced drip coffee at 85 baht and iced cocoa at 65 baht; Coffee Phi Ba listed 200 g medium-roast beans at 250 baht. Confirm current menus and prices.
hours: Saturday and Sunday. TAT lists 09:00–14:30; the market banner photographed in September 2026 showed 09:00–15:00. Plan around the earlier closing and check the market's Facebook page before leaving.
bestTime: Arrive around 09:00–10:00 for a quieter browse, more choice at food stalls and time for coffee before closing.
gettingThere: The address is 13, 16 Moo 2, Soi 11, San Klang, San Kamphaeng, Chiang Mai 50130, beside Wat Sima Ram. TAT estimates about 20 minutes by car from the Old City. Mot Dang's route estimate from Tha Phae Gate is 8.2 km/12 minutes without traffic. Use a taxi or ride-hail car and arrange the return trip; the market reports several nearby parking areas. These times are estimates, not a December traffic guarantee.
booking: No market entry reservation is listed. For current weekend operation, call the number published by TAT, 097-462-4296, or check facebook.com/ChamchaMarket. Treat individual stalls and menus as subject to change; no reservation process for café seating or market workshops was found.
accessibility: Step-free routes, accessible toilets and seating details are not published. The market has outdoor lanes and separate shop entrances, so surfaces and access may vary. Contact the market before travelling if specific access facilities are essential.
practicalTips: Use the market's Facebook page or phone number to confirm the weekend schedule shortly before your visit.
Bring small-denomination baht; individual makers and food stalls may have different payment options.
Browse first, then take a coffee break: stall choice and food availability can change during the morning.
Ask makers before photographing them or their work, and leave room for purchases.
decemberNotes: December 2026 falls in Chiang Mai's cool season, which is generally comfortable for an open-air morning, but no date-specific holiday schedule or special market event was confirmed. The regular weekend market is the best expectation; verify the chosen date and finish before the TAT-listed 14:30 closing time.
uncertainties: Closing time differs between TAT (14:30) and the market's own banner observed in September 2026 (15:00).
The September stall roster and transcribed prices may change before December; café hours outside market times were not verified.
Accessible facilities, current transport fares and December 2026 operating exceptions were not confirmed.
